drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. The revised draft reflects your proposed deletion of the non-compete and 24 months of Base Salary and continued benefits for termination without Cause or resignation for Good Reason, subject to client approval. We have proposed definitions and notice-and-cure procedures, together with express severance payment timing. Executive identity, Base Salary, and the benefits package remain open for agreement.

edits.text:
3. TERMINATION AND SEVERANCE. (a) If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay severance equal to twenty-four (24) months of Base Salary at the rate in effect immediately before termination, disregarding any reduction giving rise to Good Reason. Severance shall be paid in twenty-four (24) equal monthly installments, beginning on the thirtieth (30th) day following termination and continuing on each monthly anniversary thereafter. The Company shall also continue, for twenty-four (24) months following termination, the benefits specified in Section 2 on the same terms, including the same allocation of costs, as applied immediately before termination, disregarding any reduction giving rise to Good Reason. If continued participation is unavailable under applicable law or plan terms, the Company shall provide substantially equivalent benefits or monthly cash payments equal to the Company’s cost of providing those benefits. Earned but unpaid compensation and accrued benefits shall be paid separately in accordance with applicable law and plan terms.
(b) “Cause” means only the Executive’s fraud, embezzlement, willful misconduct, or gross negligence in performing duties, in each case causing material harm to the Company, or conviction of, or a plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony involving fraud or dishonesty. Cause does not include a good-faith business judgment or failure to meet performance expectations. Before terminating for Cause, the Company shall give written notice specifying the grounds in reasonable detail and, where curable, at least thirty (30) days to cure; if cured within that period, those grounds shall not constitute Cause.
(c) “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent, a material reduction in compensation, authority, or duties. The Executive must give written notice describing the condition within ninety (90) days after its initial occurrence, allow the Company thirty (30) days after receipt to cure, and, if uncured, resign within sixty (60) days after that cure period expires.
(d) Payments shall be administered to comply with, or qualify for an exemption from, Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code. Each installment is a separate payment. To the extent required by Section 409A, termination means a separation from service, and payments to a specified employee otherwise due during the six months following separation shall be accumulated and paid on the first business day after that period expires, or earlier upon death; remaining payments shall follow the stated schedule.
edits.name: Severance, Cause, Good Reason, and payment timing

edits.text: 4. NO NON-COMPETE. This Agreement imposes no post-employment non-competition restriction on the Executive.
edits.name: Delete post-employment non-compete

receiver.message_back: We accept the deletion of the non-compete and the 24-month severance and benefits framework, provided Good Reason also covers a material diminution in reporting status, relocation of the principal workplace by more than 50 miles, or the Company’s material breach, with notice running from the Executive’s knowledge of the condition, and any benefits cash substitute covers the Executive’s actual cost of equivalent replacement coverage rather than merely the Company’s cost. Severance must not be subject to mitigation, offset for subsequent earnings, or an additional release requirement; any final agreement remains subject to our client’s approval and agreement on Executive identity, Base Salary, and specified benefits.
